title: Ecology
seo_title: Year 11 Science: Ecology Worksheets (GCSE Combined Science)
standard_text: Communities and interdependence; abiotic and biotic factors; adaptations; levels of organisation in an ecosystem and food chains; sampling with quadrats and transects; how materials are cycled (the carbon and water cycles) and decomposition; biodiversity and the effects of human interaction on ecosystems; maintaining biodiversity.
meta_desc: Free Year 11 GCSE Combined Science worksheets on ecology: biotic and abiotic factors, adaptations, food chains, quadrats, the carbon and water cycles, biodiversity and human impacts. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Estimate a population: mean per m² × total area.
key_sub: Abiotic factors are non-living; biotic factors are living.
body_html:
How to think about it

Organisms in a community depend on each other.

  • Abiotic: light, temperature, water, pH, wind. Biotic: food, predators, pathogens, competition.
  • Quadrats: find the mean number per m², then multiply by the area.
  • Carbon is taken in by photosynthesis and returned by respiration, decay and combustion.
Example

Mean 4 daisies per m². Field 200 m²?

4 × 200

Answer: 800

Example

Is soil pH biotic or abiotic?

Not living

Answer: abiotic

Common mistakes

  • Thinking temperature is a biotic factor.
  • Using the mean per quadrat as the population.
  • Thinking all the energy passes to the next level.

faq.q: How do you estimate a population with quadrats?
faq.a: Place quadrats at random, count the organisms in each, find the mean per quadrat, then multiply by the total area (in quadrat areas).

faq.q: What is the difference between biotic and abiotic factors?
faq.a: Biotic factors are living, such as predators and food. Abiotic factors are non-living, such as light, temperature and soil pH.
High biodiversity makes ecosystems more stable, because species depend on each other for food, shelter and keeping the physical environment.

items.q: Is number of pollinators a biotic or an abiotic factor?
items.e: Abiotic factors are non-living; biotic factors are living.

items.q: An arctic fox has small ears. What type of adaptation is this?
items.e: Structural: body shape. Behavioural: how it acts. Functional: processes inside the body.

items.q: Is temperature a biotic or an abiotic factor?
items.e: Abiotic factors are non-living; biotic factors are living.

items.q: Is oxygen levels in water a biotic or an abiotic factor?
items.e: Abiotic factors are non-living; biotic factors are living.

items.q: A frog lays thousands of eggs. What type of adaptation is this?

items.q: What do animals often compete for?

items.q: A wolf eats a deer. What role do they play?

items.q: Is new pathogens a biotic or an abiotic factor?

items.q: What are extremophiles?
c: organisms that live in extreme conditions such as high temperature or salt
items.e: For example, bacteria in deep-sea vents.

items.q: Bacteria and fungi break down a fallen log. What role do they play?
items.e: Producers, consumers and decomposers.

items.q: Is carbon dioxide levels a biotic or an abiotic factor?

items.q: What is a community?

the non-living parts of a habitat
all the members of one family
items.e: A population is one species.

items.q: Hedgehogs hibernate through the winter. What type of adaptation is this?
items.e: Structural: body shape. Behavioural: how it acts. Functional: processes inside the body.

items.q: Swallows migrate south in winter. What type of adaptation is this?

items.q: What is interdependence?

items.e: Removing one species can affect the whole community.

items.q: A camel can go for days without drinking. What type of adaptation is this?

items.q: Is new predators arriving a biotic or an abiotic factor?

Does algae growing in a lake add CO<sub>2</sub> to the air or remove it?
c: It has no effect on carbon.
items.e: Photosynthesis removes CO2; respiration and burning add it.

It stays in the log forever.

items.q: Give one effect of global warming on species.

items.e: Distribution changes.

items.q: Give one way to protect biodiversity.
items.e: Also protecting habitats, hedgerows and recycling.

items.q: Plastic waste collects in the ocean. Which solution best fits this problem?

remove the invaders and check boats and cargo

items.q: Why does destroying peat bogs add to global warming?
c: Peat releases carbon dioxide when it is burned or decays.
items.e: Peat is also used as compost.
